function: Maps uplink pilots directly to RIMSA phase shifts and digital precoders for sum-rate maximization, bypassing explicit channel estimation (p. 4).
system: MISO downlink: BS with planar radiative RIS (RIMSA), 1024 metamaterial elements and 128 RF chains; 3 single-antenna users; Rician channel; frequency band not stated (p. 1, p. 8).
method: Pre-trained GPT-2 (6 layers) partially fine-tuned, attention and feed-forward frozen, plus BiLSTM, attention, residual blocks; hybrid loss of channel MSE, sum rate, zero-forcing norm (p. 5, p. 7).
data_channel: Own simulated Rician channel, LoS steering vector plus i.i.d. NLoS; 10,000 training, 2,000 validation and 5,000 test samples; no public or measured data (p. 4, p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Same simulator and random 3-user layout for training and testing; sweeps of pilot length, downlink power, users 3 to 8; no unseen condition stated (p. 8, p. 10-12).
baselines: Random RIMSA configuration (non-learned); DDPG-based DRL [32]; graph attention network GNN [28]. No optimization-based baseline is listed (p. 9).
metrics: Sum data rate and max-min data rate (bps/Hz) versus pilot length, downlink power and users; trainable parameters, training time and inference time (p. 10-12).
complexity: Table II: 1.73M trainable of 84.78M total parameters, 2.6 h training, 20 ms inference; GNN 4.8 h, 50 ms; DRL 7.3 h, 120 ms (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "Rician fading channel model"; custom simulator with path loss exponent 2.2 (p. 8); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "the number of testing samples is set as 2,000"; testing uses held-out samples of the same simulated setup. Sweeps of pilot length, power and users (p. 10 to p. 12) never say a model trained under one condition is tested under another; few-shot learning is claimed (p. 1) but not tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "No optimization: RIMSA configurations are set randomly"; p. 9: "DRL [32]: A deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG)"; p. 9: "GNN [28]: A graph attention network (GAT)"; p. 10: "evaluates the sum data rate (bps/Hz) of four" methods including random.
q4_support: p. 10: "parameters as 84.78M, the actual trainable parameters 1.73M"; p. 10: "shortest training time as 2.6 hours"; Table II on p. 10 lists 20 ms inference time.
q5_support: p. 8: "The training dataset and validation dataset respectively" contain simulated samples from the paper's own channel model (p. 4); no code or data link, DOI, or public dataset appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (Aug 2025) of 'LLM-RIMSA: Large Language Models driven Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurface Antenna Systems' (p. 1); it prints no DOI, so identity rests on title and topic. The text layer of p. 3 is garbled (overlapping text from another document), so I read the rendered page 3: it holds the end of the contribution list, Fig. 1, Fig. 2 and Section II-A, with nothing on code, data or baselines. Eligibility: the learned GPT-2 network outputs the RIMSA phase matrix V and the digital precoder W (p. 5, p. 8), so it passes learning, layer, function and system checks; simulation results are on p. 10 to p. 12. Area 3: the main metric is the sum rate (p. 5); the channel estimation head is an auxiliary output (p. 8 'Channel estimation head'). ris is 1 because the paper defines RIMSA as 'a novel radiative RIS architecture' (p. 1), although here it is the BS antenna and not a reflecting surface; the reviewer should confirm. The carrier frequency is never given. The dataset sizes are inconsistent: p. 8-9 say 10,000 training, 2,000 validation and 5,000 test samples, while p. 10 says 10,000, 1,000 and 2,000. q3: the learned baselines are DDPG and graph attention network designs adapted by the authors; p. 8 announces a comparison with 'the channel estimation based approach', but none appears in the baseline list on p. 9, and Fig. 8 (p. 11) omits the random baseline. q2: the network input depends on the pilot length (p. 7) and the output on the number of users (p. 8), and Fig. 11 (p. 12) shows separate training curves per pilot length, which points to retraining for each setting, but the paper does not state it.
